data.Description: Terry Kanmacher was allegedly trying to flee the U.S. after killing a woman with whom he'd had a brief relationship.
data.Story:
A 21-year-old French man who’s suspected of killing a woman in Nebraska was arrested Tuesday evening at Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport before he could board a return flight to France.

Agents with Homeland Security Investigations took Terry Kanmacher, a French national, into custody while he attempted to go through airport security, according to Nebraska’s Omaha Police Department.

Police believe Kanmacher stabbed 22-year-old Lauren Becker, an employee of the Kids Can Community Center in Omaha, Nebraska, while she was walking into work Tuesday morning. She was pronounced dead in the facility’s parking lot.

Investigators determined that Kanmacher and Becker had a brief romantic relationship several years ago, and the two only met once in 2023, then Becker broke it off. She eventually reported to police that she was afraid of Kanmacher.

According to Omaha PD, Kanmacher traveled to Nebraska on Sunday and originally planned to return to France next week, but he abruptly moved up his flight and drove to Minnesota for its departure roughly 12 hours after Becker was killed.

Kanmacher is currently being held in the Hennepin County Jail, but he will eventually be extradited to Nebraska to face charges.

“I extend my deepest condolences to the family and friends of Lauren Becker during this difficult time. I commend Omaha Police Department detectives and our federal partners with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) for their decisive and diligent actions in securing an arrest. Working against the clock as the investigation unfolded, they stopped at nothing to bring this individual into custody,” Omaha Police Chief Todd Schmaderer said in a statement.

If you know anyone who is affected by domestic violence, you can find more information on services available here, via the Minnesota DPS. You can also call the Day One Crisis Hotline at 1-866-223-1111.

Note: The details provided in this story are based on law enforcement’s latest version of events, and may be subject to change.
